overview: Veralto is a global analytics and technology company spun off from Danaher Corporation in September 2023, operating under the purpose of "Safeguarding the World's Most Vital Resources." The company provides water quality testing, treatment and digital monitoring solutions (Hach, ChemTreat, Trojan Technologies) and product quality/traceability solutions for consumer packaged goods, food & beverage, and pharmaceutical customers (Videojet, Linx, Esko, X-Rite, Pantone). Veralto generates roughly $5.5 billion in annual revenue, operates globally (about 56% of sales outside the U.S.), and runs its businesses using the Veralto Enterprise System (VES), a continuous-improvement management framework inherited from its former parent's Danaher Business System.

business_model.summary: Veralto sells a mix of analytical instruments, treatment equipment and marking/coding hardware alongside high-margin, recurring consumables (reagents, chemicals, inks, spare parts), software and services. Roughly 61% of revenue is recurring, giving the model an installed-base/razor-razorblade characteristic similar to its former Danaher parent.

revenue_streams.name: Product Quality & Innovation (Videojet, Linx, Esko, X-Rite, Pantone)

business_model.customer_type: B2B - municipal water utilities, industrial water users (power, mining, chemicals, data centers), consumer packaged goods companies, food & beverage manufacturers, and pharmaceutical companies; no single customer exceeds 10% of sales
business_model.geographic_mix: North America ~48%, Western Europe ~23%, other developed markets ~2%, high-growth/emerging markets ~27% (including China, which has been a soft spot in municipal water funding)

main_competitors: Danaher (Videojet's former sibling units and legacy overlap)
competitive_position.market_position: Holds #1 or #2 share positions in most of the niche markets it serves; Hach is a leading brand in water analytics/testing across roughly 150 countries, and Videojet/X-Rite/Pantone hold leading positions in industrial coding/marking and color management respectively.

moat_factors.description: ~61% of revenue from reagents, chemicals, inks, spare parts and software tied to a large installed base, producing high visibility and stickiness
Hach, ChemTreat, Videojet, X-Rite/Pantone are category-defining brands relied upon in regulated, safety-critical water and product-quality applications
Customers standardize on proprietary instrumentation/software and calibrated consumables, raising the cost/risk of switching vendors in regulated environments
Continuous-improvement culture inherited from Danaher Business System supports above-peer margins (~24% adjusted operating margin vs. ~15-18% industrial peer range) and disciplined M&A integration
Global service and distribution footprint supports faster response times than smaller regional competitors

weaknesses: Faces large, well-capitalized competitors (Xylem, Pentair, Ecolab) in water, and some fragmented low-cost competition in product marking/coding
China municipal water demand has been structurally weak, pressuring Water Quality segment growth in that region
PQI segment exposed to industrial/packaging production volumes, which can be more cyclical than Water Quality's project/consumable base
Relatively short track record as a standalone public company (spun off September 2023) limits historical data for investors

growth_drivers: Secular water scarcity, aging infrastructure and tightening water-quality regulation support long-term demand for Hach testing instruments and Trojan/ChemTreat treatment solutions
Data center buildout driving industrial water treatment and cooling-water analytics demand (cited explicitly in Q2 2026 results)

Bolt-on M&A strategy adding capability and geographic reach: GlobalVision (AI packaging quality/compliance software, March 2026), Alfaa UV (Indian UV water treatment, mid-2026), and the pending ~$465 million Cleanwater1 acquisition (on-site disinfection/odor control, expected to close Q4 2026)
AI-enabled software and digital workflow tools in PQI (Esko, GlobalVision) supporting packaging compliance and brand integrity for CPG/pharma customers
Continued adjusted operating margin expansion (~25-50 bps guided for FY2026) from VES-driven productivity and pricing
Capital return program (ongoing share buybacks - over 5 million shares, ~$480 million repurchased in Q2 2026 alone) supporting EPS growth

business.description: Operates in markets with a wide range of competitors from regional players to large diversified corporations (Xylem, Pentair, Ecolab), with pricing and innovation pressure
High-growth markets were roughly flat in Q2 2026 with some shrinkage in Water segment China sales tied to weak municipal funding
Product Quality & Innovation segment tied to packaging/industrial production volumes, which can soften with weaker consumer or industrial demand
Active bolt-on M&A pipeline (GlobalVision, Alfaa UV, Cleanwater1) requires successful integration to realize synergies

financial.description: ChemTreat chemical input costs have been volatile, pressuring segment margins and requiring pricing offsets
~56% of sales generated outside the U.S. creates translation and transaction currency risk
Significant goodwill and intangibles from the Danaher spin-off and subsequent acquisitions create impairment risk if end markets deteriorate

regulatory.description: Extensive regulatory regimes govern water quality, chemicals handling, and product safety/traceability, raising compliance costs but also underpinning demand
Tariff exposure affecting supply chains and costs, with uncertain timing of potential tariff refunds flagged by management in 2026
GDPR and other data privacy frameworks, plus export/import control compliance for global operations

macro.description: Water Quality's municipal customer base is sensitive to government/municipal capital budgets, which can be deferred in weak macro environments
Industrial water treatment and PQI packaging/coding volumes correlate with broader industrial and consumer production activity
Moderate direct exposure; higher rates could raise financing costs for M&A and buybacks and pressure customer capital spending

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global demand for water testing, treatment and product traceability is supported by tightening regulation, water scarcity, aging infrastructure, and growing need for supply-chain/brand integrity in consumer goods and pharma; water quality end markets are viewed as a long-duration secular growth category
macro_factors.cyclicality: Water Quality segment is relatively defensive (regulatory/consumable-driven); Product Quality & Innovation is more cyclical, tied to packaging/industrial production and CPG volumes
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-to-moderate - primarily indirect via customer capital spending (municipal and industrial) and the company's own M&A/buyback financing costs

recent_developments.event: Announced definitive agreement to acquire Cleanwater1 for approximately $465 million; adds on-site hypochlorite disinfection, solids management and odor filtration technologies (~25,000 installed units, ~$135M LTM sales); expected to close Q4 2026

Reported Q2 2026 results: sales up 7.6% YoY to $1,474M, non-GAAP core sales growth 4.2% (Water Quality +5.7%, PQI +2%); adjusted EPS of $1.11, up 19.4% YoY; raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $4.35-$4.43 (12-14% growth); repurchased over 5 million shares for ~$480 million in the quarter
Acquired Alfaa UV, an Indian ultraviolet water treatment company, to be integrated into Trojan Technologies to expand UV water treatment reach in India/emerging markets

Announced acquisition of GlobalVision (Montreal-based AI-augmented packaging quality/compliance software) to be integrated into Esko, alongside completion of $300 million in share repurchases; GlobalVision projected ~$25M 2026 sales with ~85% recurring revenue
Q1 2026 results showed ~7% sales growth and ~13% adjusted EPS growth, prompting an initial raise to full-year EPS outlook

Continued softness in China municipal water funding and broader high-growth-market water demand, partially offset by data center-driven industrial water treatment demand and steady PQI coding/digital workflow demand

items.notes: Represents 12-14% YoY growth; raised following strong Q1 and Q2 results
Full-year range; second-half core revenue growth projected at 5-6%, implying acceleration into H2
Q3 guided at ~25 bps expansion; Q4 expected to show larger uplift driven by PQI production efficiencies
Quarterly guidance issued alongside Q2 2026 results

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Jennifer Honeycutt highlighted sequential acceleration in both segments, with Water Quality strength driven by data center and industrial water scarcity demand, and PQI supported by digital workflow software. CFO Sameer Ralhan flagged volatile ChemTreat raw material costs, expected pricing moderation, and uncertain timing on potential tariff refunds as factors to watch, while reaffirming confidence in sequential margin improvement through year-end.

bull_case: High-margin recurring revenue (~61% of sales) from consumables, software and service tied to a large global installed base provides earnings visibility and resilience
Secular tailwinds from water scarcity, tightening water-quality regulation, and growing packaging/traceability compliance needs support durable long-term demand
Active, disciplined bolt-on M&A pipeline (GlobalVision, Alfaa UV, Cleanwater1) adds capability and growth without large integration risk, funded by strong free cash flow
Veralto Enterprise System (inherited from Danaher) drives above-peer margins (~24% adjusted operating margin) and consistent productivity gains, with further expansion guided for FY2026
Raised FY2026 EPS guidance (12-14% growth) and accelerating core sales growth into H2 2026 signal positive earnings momentum; substantial share buybacks further support EPS growth
bear_case: Stock has underperformed since the 2023 spinoff and is down roughly 9% over the trailing year as of late 2026 despite earnings beats, suggesting valuation/sentiment headwinds
China and other high-growth-market water demand remains structurally weak due to municipal funding constraints, a drag on the larger Water Quality segment
PQI segment's exposure to industrial/packaging production volumes makes it more sensitive to a broader industrial or consumer slowdown
Volatile raw material costs (notably in ChemTreat) and tariff/trade policy uncertainty create margin and cost unpredictability
Intensifying competition from larger, diversified players (Xylem, Pentair, Ecolab) could pressure pricing and share in core water and product-quality markets
